newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ATA pins hopes on training to save wheat futures.
newsitem.headline: ATA pins hopes on training to save wheat futures.

text.p: Amsterdam's Agricultural Futures Exchange (ATA) said on Friday a lack of market volatility was behind its wheat contract attracting such a low turnover but added it was pinning its hopes on a Europe-wide training programme to drum up fresh business.
"Market volatility, or lack of it, is the problem but education is another key factor," exchange spokesman Kasper Wallet told Reuters at the European Commodities Exchange.
The ATA said it was concentrating on convincing farmers and smaller traders of the need for a European bread wheat contract.
It said the market was just getting underway in Europe.

The exchange has been engaged in a consultation process with potential users for the last month in a bid to revive interest in the contract, which has fallen well short of expectations since its launch this summer.
Trade sources at the conference were sceptical that a training programme alone would solve the problem.
"You need big volumes for a contract to survive and for that you need the big trading houses. They already know about trading," one said.
"Maybe it's a timing problem. The interest is there but it probably needs the market to hot up a little," he added.
